title: Random-forest screening identifies a breast-cancer growth-suppressing role for PCAT19
summary: A random-forest survival model helped prioritize lncRNAs from 1054 breast-cancer expression profiles; overlap with differential expression and a separate expression database nominated PCAT19. Knocking down PCAT19 increased proliferation in two breast-cancer cell lines, while overexpression reduced xenograft growth in mice. The work supports a preclinical growth-suppressing role, not a validated treatment. Predicted regulatory networks remain hypotheses, and inconsistent clinical-prognosis wording is not used to establish patient benefit.

evidence.tested: Random-forest prioritization was followed by PCAT19 knockdown in two breast-cancer cell lines and overexpression in a mouse xenograft model, supporting an effect on growth. Migration and invasion changes were not statistically significant.
evidence.unknown: No clinical intervention or treatment benefit is established. The paper contains inconsistent directions in its clinical-prognosis narrative and reports 151 versus 153 tissue cases in different sections; these clinical claims are not represented as validated findings. The proposed ceRNA network remains computational.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest survival feature importance selected the top 10% of lncRNAs from 1054 TCGA breast-cancer profiles; intersection with differential expression and external expression evidence helped select PCAT19 for functional experiments.

source_review.scope: Exact article-front DOI/title/PMCID and publication date; full primary Methods, Results and limitations. Admission represents the model-prioritized experimental growth result; contradictory clinical prognosis descriptions are explicitly excluded from the claim.
